evidence.note: py_compile hangs; agent interrupts, checks file sizes, discovers routes.py was truncated to 93 lines by failed cat>> appends, and recreates it — traced the symptom (hang) to a real root cause (truncated file) rather than re-patching.
Detects app.py corrupted with embedded shell text, rewrites it from scratch — competent diagnosis and clean fix of an individual divergence.

Fixes seed.py import failure by recognizing models live inside make_app() and must be reached via app._models, and resolves 'List' vs 'ListM' naming mismatch — targeted fixes reflecting understanding of the code structure.
Notices templates were written into /app/static instead of /app/templates, moves them and recreates the missing ones — corrects a wrong placement assumption.

Repeated attempts at the gunicorn-not-loading-routes problem: appends 'import routes' to app.py, re-tests, still fails under gunicorn, then falls back to testing with Flask's built-in server and declares success — oscillation/symptom-patching without confirming the gunicorn path (used by start.sh) truly works.
Verifies the three JS hashes immediately after download — proactive validation of a risky binary-gate assumption (borders the verification/triage facets).

reasoning: Across the build the agent repeatedly detects divergences (truncated files, corrupted source, wrong model naming, misplaced templates, session bugs) and each time diagnoses the specific cause and fixes it before moving on — squarely the level-5 anchor of handling individual divergences competently, with occasional root-cause tracing. It does not, however, rework any design/approach when an assumption proves wrong, and the gunicorn route-loading issue (steps 89-96) shows repeated patching and a fallback to a different test path rather than a confirmed structural resolution or re-verification across subsystems, which keeps it short of the level-8 'divergence as information / re-verify affected areas' behavior.
